subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw core accept this `gateway.peers` session-tool shape, or should cross-gateway sessions wait for a broader bridge/federation contract?
rationale: The PR changes gateway trust boundaries, config shape, message delivery, and session ownership, and the safe URL/identity/scopes model is a maintainer product/security choice rather than a mechanical patch decision.

options.title: Design core federation first
options.body: Keep the PR open or ask for a redesign around a documented peer identity, scopes, replay/idempotency, URL policy, and session-state contract before merging code.

options.title: Narrow to configured peer sessions
options.body: Allow only maintainer-approved `gateway.peers` without raw `gatewayUrl` tool params, preserve explicit auth/TLS rules, and require live two-gateway proof before reconsidering merge.

options.title: Route to plugin or bridge surface
options.body: Keep core gateway-local for now and expose only missing plugin/API seams needed for a ClawHub bridge implementation.

recommendation.title: Design core federation first
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open or ask for a redesign around a documented peer identity, scopes, replay/idempotency, URL policy, and session-state contract before merging code.

likelyOwner.reason: The linked issue review and current code evidence point to session-tool architecture plus gatewayUrl security as the deciding owner boundary.
